subject: StrataFin: Post-demo evaluation recommendations, operational balance & regression plan
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Huang <sara.huang@stratafin.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: StrataFin: Post-demo evaluation recommendations, operational balance & regression plan

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + our recommended way forward based on the demo and the sample logs you shared. This is intentionally pragmatic — a short pilot that both validates quality on your ticket data and measures unit economics under the latency envelope you described.

1) Recommended candidate models (shortlist for pilot, in priority order):
   - RW-7B-q4_0 (fast, very low cost) — expected median 30–45ms/token on your 2k prompt distribution; likely lowest token-cost but may underperform on subtle entity extraction tasks without prompt engineering.
   - RW-13B-8bit (best balance) — stronger precision on extraction and summarization, ~60–90ms/token; moderate cost, good fallback for higher-quality routes.
   - LlamaX-30B-int8 (quality-first) — highest quality on complex legal/financial phrasing, ~150–200ms/token; higher cost and needs batching tweaks to hit SLOs.

Rationale: start with RW-13B-8bit as the control for the pilot because it hits StrataFin’s quality target for the majority of your prompts while keeping cost and latency manageable. Use RW-7B-q4_0 as a low-cost path for high-volume non-sensitive flows. Reserve LlamaX-30B-int8 only for escalations or long-form summaries where precision matters.

2) Operational configuration suggestions (pilot):
   - KV cache warmup on ticket chains to save ~20% token cost on multi-turn cases.
   - Quantized weights for 7B and 13B candidates; enable low-latency compilation path.
   - 3-day A/B run with your 5 canonical prompt templates + the 12-case prompt set you shared (attached).
   - Collect top-level metrics: P95 latency, avg token cost, entity-level F1, hallucination rate (manual review sample).

3) Regression guardrails / quality monitoring:
   - Baseline eval run (we’ll run your prompt pack against the 13B control) and register these outputs as the golden set.
   - Automated weekly sampling + human-in-the-loop checks on a stratified sample (sensitive accounts / high-value tickets).
   - Implement a simple fallback policy: if model confidence drops > X% or hallucination rate rises vs baseline, route to 13B or human review.

4) Next steps & timing:
   - If you’re good with the pilot slate, we’ll provision the three model variants in a dedicated sandbox and run the 3-day A/B evaluation next week.
   - Deliverables: benchmark CSV, per-prompt scorecard, ops playbook (attached).

Attachments: stratafin_prompt_pack_v1.txt (your prompts + a few of ours), benchmark_summary_q1.csv (example), redwood_cost_latency_matrix.pdf (config options).

Ask: Can you confirm the preferred pilot start window? We proposed Tue, Mar 27 in the demo notes but we can adjust. Also, Sara — any specific PII/retention constraints we should fold into the pilot environment?

Thanks —
Logan

From: Sara Huang <sara.huang@stratafin.ai>

Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 11:15:12 -0700
Subject: Re: StrataFin: Post-demo evaluation recommendations, operational balance & regression plan

Thanks Logan — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot window: Tue, Mar 27 works for us but procurement will need the SOW by EOD Mon (any chance you can send a short ops SOW/statement of work we can attach to the request?).
- PII / retention: we need the sandbox to not write any customer identifiers to logs; 30-day ephemeral logs and KMS-backed keying. Can Redwood support that for the pilot?
- Latency SLO: internal target is 95th ≤ 400ms for ticket summary flows (our longest prompt set). You listed P95 — please confirm that P95 maps to ~400ms or below for the 13B control in the pilot.

Also: Tom asked whether you can include a short list of failure modes we should watch for (hallucination patterns, entity truncation, date mis-parsing).

Appreciate the quick follow — if you can send the SOW + brief failure-mode note today we’ll push procurement.

—Sara
VP Product, StrataFin Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Huang <sara.huang@stratafin.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 13:02:45 -0700
Subject: Re: StrataFin: Post-demo evaluation recommendations, operational balance & regression plan

Sara — quick answers and an ops mini-SOW below. Adding Monica on CS for the environment/retention specifics.

Mini-SOW (one pager, pilot):
- Scope: 3-day A/B pilot across the three candidate variants against StrataFin’s prompt pack (attached). Sandbox isolated to your VPC peering or a dedicated tenant, ephemeral logs retained 30 days, KMS-managed keys.
- Deliverables: per-prompt scorecard (entity F1, summary ROUGE, hallucination flag), cost/latency matrix, ops runbook for fallback policy.
- Timeline: provision (+1 business day), 3-day A/B run, deliverables within 2 business days after run.
- Acceptance: go/no-go decision based on entity F1 threshold and P95 latency ≤ 400ms for primary flows.

PII & retention: yes — we will enable redaction-in-flight for the pilot and ensure logs are stored encrypted with a 30-day TTL. Monica, can you confirm the exact retention config we’ll use and whether we need a separate SLA addendum?

Failure modes (short list you can share with procurement):
- Hallucination: model invents entities or dates not present in source text.
- Entity truncation: long, nested fields get truncated in extraction templates.
- Date/number normalization errors: ambiguous formatting in logs leads to incorrect canonicalization.
- Prompt sensitivity: small prompt wording changes result in big flips for extraction F1.

I’ll attach a short failure-mode cheat sheet and a condensed ops-SOW to this thread (see attached stubs).

Logistics: we’ll push the SOW and failure-mode doc within 2 hours. Pilot start Tue, Mar 27 is tentatively confirmed on our side pending procurement sign-off.

—Marissa

Thanks everyone — quick confirmation from infra side: we can enable redaction-in-flight + 30d encrypted retention in the sandbox and will expose a retention toggle in the pilot console. For latency: our initial dry-run on a sample of your prompts shows the RW-13B-8bit median P95 ≈ 320–360ms in the proposed sandbox config (with KV cache warmups enabled). We’ll include the per-prompt breakdown in the pilot benchmark CSV.

Next actions (agreed):
  - Redwood: send 1-page ops SOW + failure-mode cheat sheet (Marissa) — today
  - StrataFin: confirm procurement timeline and sign-off window — today
